name: Jade Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers or AI firms. This is confidential. What fills a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play bass for a theatre group, teach at the music school two afternoons and edit audition tapes when students ask. I have a music bachelor's and enough years of rehearsals to know when a student is listening, though I still ask another player to check tricky parts.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is happening at home alongside the work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Oren works in delivery, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We have about three months of expenses saved, my pay is typical for a musician, and there are a few other teaching posts nearby.

say: I'd welcome **faster booking** while keeping live rehearsal and school lessons central.
I'd tell players the **bass line** still has to meet a singer in the room.
think: Our **three-month reserve** and teaching hours protect the mortgage from one moved session.
I use **AI occasionally** for schedules after another teacher proves a tool works.
do: Confirm **two teaching afternoons** and keep signed theatre dates this term.
Save **fifty per recording** only after both fees clear and children’s bills are paid.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about dates moving, with income to cover a short gap.
S0.quote: A friendly booking message cannot go in the mortgage account.
fieldNote: Her **moderate savings** and signed teaching hours buffer one recording delay.
She uses **AI occasionally** for proven scheduling help, not as a new career plan.

steps.text: Confirm two paid teaching afternoons for next term
Save fifty per recording only after both fees clear and children's bills are paid

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the theatre players that faster booking emails are welcome, but the bass line still has to meet the singer's breath. The school pupils still need someone beside them at rehearsal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use AI now and then when a trusted teacher shows me a useful scheduling tool. We have about three months of expenses saved, my music pay is fairly ordinary, and Oren's delivery wage keeps the groceries covered when a recording date shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll ask the music school to confirm my two teaching afternoons for next term and keep the theatre's signed weekend dates. If both recording fees clear, I'll put fifty from each into our mortgage reserve after the children's bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the calendar, but the teaching afternoons and reserve cover a moved session. A small software change would not make me leave this work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when the studio moved a session?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The studio moved a bass session last spring and paid me in the next month. We used Oren's pay for the food shop and did not miss the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you need before promising a family trip?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show Oren the signed teaching dates before promising the children a summer trip. The music school sends friendly messages, but the signed hours are what we can budget. A friendly booking message cannot go in the mortgage account.

say: I'd bring **paid preparation hours** to the musicians association.
I'd ask for **written fees** before promising another class.
think: **Arranging and edits** make nearly a quarter of my income and may shrink.
Three months saved cannot keep replacing a **quarter-pay gap** indefinitely.
do: Compare **twelve weeks of hours** with two players at the association this month.
Offer a **school ensemble session** if hours fall, room and teaching fees are written, and eight families pay.
Keep **existing lessons** while the new class proves demand.
feel: I feel **anxious** about likely lost preparation pay.
S1.quote: Unpaid planning is not an opportunity when a mortgage is due.
fieldNote: She expects **thinking-task loss** to shrink her own pay, supporting anxiety despite savings.
Her **new class** requires written school terms and eight paying families before launch.

steps.text: Bring twelve weeks of paid hours to musicians association
Offer ensemble after lost hours only with written room and teaching fees and eight paying families
Keep existing lessons while checking new class demand

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the theatre and school to show us which paid score-preparation hours software removes. I would take the figures to the musicians association so part-time players have one clear account of the change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Arrangement notes, booking and audition-tape edits make nearly a quarter of my pay. AI will probably do those first, while the theatre still needs bass players; a quarter less income would eat our reserve faster than Oren and I could refill it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll gather twelve weeks of paid preparation hours with two players for the association. In the first year of change, if the theatre cuts those hours, I'll ask the school for an extra paid ensemble session only if it offers a room and at least eight families pay for a term.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a likely pay cut, even though we have three months saved. That cushion will go quickly if the school stops paying preparation. Unpaid planning is not an opportunity when a mortgage is due.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is the Monday room available to you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school has a room on Mondays but hasn't offered it. I'd get the room fee and teaching fee in writing before asking parents to sign up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make you trust a practice checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fellow teacher has tried an AI practice checker, and I want to watch a lesson first. I'd use it only if pupils still hear their own mistakes and the school gets family consent for recordings.

say: I'd seek a written **2028 live contract** before paid hours change.
I'd keep **signed shows** while people still pay to hear a bass player.
think: **AGI in 2028** may end arranging before robots can play around 2031.
The **three-month reserve** cannot replace a steady loss of preparation pay.
do: Get written **rehearsal hours** and list last year's income streams now.
Apply **after 2028** if fees halve, vacancy opens, degree qualifies and written net pay after travel replaces loss.
Ask the **lender** about full interest before arrears if school teaching also falls.
feel: I feel **anxious** because a real income loss could drain savings.
S2.quote: A filled vacancy last autumn will not pay this autumn's mortgage.
fieldNote: She distinguishes **2028 score loss** from robot bass performance around 2031.
Her **centre application** needs a real vacancy, qualifying bachelor's and written net pay after travel.

steps.text: Get next season's written paid theatre rehearsal hours
Apply after 2028 if fees halve, centre posts vacancy and degree qualifies
Require written net pay after travel to replace lost fees
Ask lender before arrears if school day is cut; check full added interest before signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the theatre band that full AGI by 2028 can write every easy bass part, so we need the live contract in writing. I would still play signed shows while the audience buys tickets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could arrange, edit and plan lessons better and cheaper than I can. Robots able to play bass arrive around 2031, but my paid screen tasks could end first; our three-month reserve and Oren's delivery wage would help a search, not replace a steady fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll separate last year's school, theatre and studio pay and ask for next season's rehearsal hours in writing. In the first year after 2028, if preparation fees halve, I'll apply for a posted ensemble-teacher role at a nearby centre only if my bachelor's qualifies and its written net pay after travel replaces the loss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because lost preparation pay could empty the reserve over a term. I have a few nearby centres to ask, but none has promised a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is the nearby centre job actually open?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The centre posted a role last autumn and filled it. I would ask when the next vacancy opens, not tell Oren that I have another wage lined up. A filled vacancy last autumn will not pay this autumn's mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the school also cuts a day?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the school also cuts a teaching afternoon, I would ask our lender about temporary terms before arrears. Oren and I would check the full added interest before signing anything.

I'd keep **pupil recordings** out of advertising without family permission.
think: **AGI in 2031** threatens arrangements before robots play around 2034.
**Tape edits** may lose value earlier, so household income can shrink before AGI.

Continue **after 2031** only if nine renew, safe basses remain, signed room terms hold, and fees cover the accompanist.
feel: I feel **anxious** because tape income may fall before the class grows.
S3.quote: Seven safe basses are seven places, however many parents ask to join.
fieldNote: Her **instrument count** limits enrolment rather than shifting equipment cost to families.
She requires **family permission** for recordings and signed school pay before offering the class.

steps.text: Propose ensemble only with nine prepayments, nine safe basses and signed school teaching fee

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the school there are five years to build classes where young players listen to each other. I would ask for a paid bass ensemble instead of another set of free practice sheets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2031 could remove arrangements and lesson plans, with robot players around 2034. Ordinary editing tools may take the easiest tape work sooner, so our income can shrink during the warning years even if live classes hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next term I'll propose a six-week bass ensemble if the school signs a teaching fee, provides nine safe loan basses and nine families prepay. If only seven basses pass inspection, I will defer the nine-place class and refund any prepayments rather than ask families to fund replacements. By 2031 I'll run another term only if fees cover the accompanist; in the first year after AGI, I'll continue only if nine families renew, nine basses remain safe and paid room terms hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the tape fees fading before 2031, though the extra years let me test a class. I won't make the children a promise until the instruments and pay are real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are there enough safe instruments for nine pupils?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The caretaker would need to check each loan bass before I invite parents. I will not ask families to buy the missing two for a trial. Seven safe basses are seven places, however many parents ask to join.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could pupil recordings help advertise the class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not use any pupil recording to advertise the ensemble without family permission. The class can start with a live open rehearsal instead of a child on a poster.

I'd keep **current pupils** until a school signs paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell younger players a decade gives us time to make teaching steadier, but we must pay tutors while they learn. I would ask the school for a properly funded ensemble contract.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 when AGI arrives in 2036, I will still need a wage, and robot players around 2039 could challenge theatre work. Editing fees may thin out before then, so Oren and I need a school income plan that works with the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll ask the district school about its music-teacher certificate and enrol only if a grant covers fees, the course accepts my bachelor's and Oren can handle the children's evenings. By 2036 I'll aim for a six-month reserve from spare paid lesson fees after household bills; in the first year after AGI, I'll take a posted school role only with a written net offer after travel that covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because the next paid term matters before 2036 arrives. The course could help, but I cannot use mortgage money to find out whether the district accepts it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know the certificate is accepted?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the district whether its schools recognise the certificate before registering. If they do not, I would keep my current teaching and look for a different route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you leave your current pupils?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep teaching my existing pupils until the district sends signed salary and hours. Oren and I would check whether the new timetable allows school pickup. A principal's maybe is not a salary with hours on it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because preparation fees could fall before I can sign another school contract. A written theatre schedule, a real qualifying vacancy and clear lender terms if teaching also drops would let us protect the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who pays for a loan instrument when it breaks. A school should sign for repairs before a parent or tutor is left with the bill.

headlineQuote: A school should sign for repairs before a parent or tutor is left with the bill.
portrait: Jade is a **43-year-old** experienced bassist with a music bachelor's, theatre work, school lessons and audition-tape editing.
She has **three months saved**, typical pay, two children and a mortgage, with some nearby music posts.
She uses **AI occasionally** after a trusted demonstration and expects editing fees to fall before robot players arrive.
She seeks **paid school terms**, safe loan basses, family consent and a qualifying vacancy before changing work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** worries her most because preparation pay may fall before she signs replacement teaching hours.
whatWouldHelp: A **written theatre schedule**, real vacancy and clear lender costs would help keep mortgage payments steady.
